findings.title: All slice-design success criteria are covered by tasks
findings.description:
Cross-referenced each of the seven success criteria in the slice design:

- SC1 (five `cf_*` names registered + load-time validation): Task 6.4 (registration + import), Task 7.1 (`test_all_five_registered`), Task 7.4 (pipeline-surface test with `cf_bogus` rejection), Task 9.1 step 1.
- SC2 (mocked-transport arg mapping + result mapping): Task 7.2 (per-tool arg mapping), Task 7.3 (transport result pass-through), Task 5.1 (echo + isError + empty mapping in the bridge).
- SC3 (real stdio round-trip, server isError, timeout, WARNING): Task 5.1 (`test_echo_round_trip`, `test_server_is_error_*`), Task 5.2 (timeout + child-process reaped), Task 5.4 (caplog WARNING assertions).
- SC4 (spawn failure → is_error + WARNING, no exception): Task 5.3 + Task 5.4.
- SC5 (live contract test): Task 8 (availability gate, `list_tools()` over the real session, schema-name assertions reading constants from `cf_tools`).
- SC6 (live demo): Task 9.1 step 2 (`cf_workflow_status` smoke from repo root) and Task 8.2 (one live round-trip). The non-SDK dispatch half of SC6 is intentionally deferred — the slice design's walkthrough §4 itself is marked "Draft — refined after Phase 6" and the `sq run` CLAUDECODE guard is acknowledged in Task 9.3 ("remains open alongside 263's demo"). This is a pre-existing design constraint, not a task-breakdown gap.
- SC7 (full suite green, pyright zero, ruff clean): Task 9.2.

findings.title: Sequencing respects dependencies and test-with pattern
findings.description: Order is config keys → config tests → fake MCP fixture → bridge impl → bridge tests → descriptors → descriptor tests → live contract test → walkthrough/close-out. Test tasks (2, 5, 7, 8) each immediately follow their implementation task (1, 4, 6, 6 respectively). No circular dependencies. The fixture (Task 3) precedes every test that uses it. Layering invariant `cf_tools → mcp_bridge` is asserted both in the bridge's success criteria and in Task 6's success criteria.

findings.title: Commit markers are at working, tested points
findings.description: Each of the nine tasks has a plain-line `**Commit**:` marker (no checkboxes) tied to a real commit message, placed after the task's scoped tests have run. Distribution is even: config feat/test, fixture test, bridge feat/test, descriptors feat/test, contract test, docs. Not bunched at the end.

findings.title: No scope creep outside success criteria
findings.description: All non-test tasks trace directly to success criteria or to the implementation surface the design enumerates (§ Files changed): `mcp_bridge.py`, `cf_tools.py`, `tools/__init__.py` edit, and `config/keys.py`. The fake-server fixture (Task 3) and config-key tests (Task 2) are required scaffolding called out by the design ("Test infrastructure first: tasks 5, 6 both need a real stdio peer"), not scope creep. The verification walkthrough (Task 9) and merge step (9.4) are standard Phase 6 close-out, not new requirements.

findings.title: "Prefer" wording understates the DRY rule for the executor builder
findings.description: Task 6.2 says "Prefer one shared executor-builder parameterized by the mapping-table entry over five hand-written near-identical closures (DRY)". CLAUDE.md states "Do not duplicate logic. Respect DRY" as a core principle, not a preference. A junior implementer reading "prefer" may reasonably produce five near-identical closures that satisfy the letter of the task. Tightening to "Build one shared executor-builder... do not write five near-identical closures" would make the expectation unambiguous. This is a wording nit, not a blocking issue — the surrounding bullets and the mapping-table requirement already push toward the right design.

findings.title: Live contract test partially duplicates walkthrough step 2
findings.description: Task 8.2's live `cf_workflow_status` round-trip and Task 9.1's walkthrough step 2 both materialize `cf_workflow_status` and invoke it from the repo root. They serve different purposes (Task 8 = pytest assertion as part of the contract test; Task 9 = recorded manual walkthrough outcome), so the duplication is intentional, but a junior AI may wonder whether to fold them. No action required; flagging for awareness.

findings.title: Proportionality is appropriate for the slice size
findings.description: Nine tasks for two new product files (~80 + ~150 lines), one edited `__init__.py`, two config keys, and four test files. Test granularity matches the design's explicit test inventory (argument-mapping units, real stdio round-trip, failure-mode coverage, availability-gated contract test) with no excess. No load test required — the slice design does not restate any NFR that would warrant one in `tests/load/`.
